ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two right triangles in the figure. The triangle on the left is ABD, AB is the vertical side and is labeled 3, there is a right-angle mark at B, and BD is the base; the triangle on the right is FEC, EF is the vertical side and is labeled 8, there is a right-angle mark at E, and EC is the base. The text in the figure gives BD = x - 1 and CE = x + 2. Angle A and angle F have the same arc marks, indicating that they are equal. Reasoning: Because triangle ABD and triangle FEC are both right triangles, and ∠A ≅ ∠F, the two triangles are similar by AA. The corresponding sides are AB ↔ FE and BD ↔ EC, therefore BD/EC = AB/FE = 3/8. Substituting BD = x - 1 and EC = x + 2 gives (x - 1)/(x + 2) = 3/8. Cross-multiplying: 8(x - 1) = 3(x + 2), that is, 8x - 8 = 3x + 6, so 5x = 14, x = 2.8. Therefore EC = x + 2 = 2.8 + 2 = 4.8.
